stock.name: Hinge Health, Inc.
stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on revenue growth, trailing year, six-month return against spy, operating margin trend — revenue +49.9% over the trailing year, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield
evidence.period: trailing year against the reference close

stock.peerBasis: 105 candidates in SIC major group 73, compared on free cash flow yield, all from the same source and the same periods.

runnersUp.name: e.l.f. Beauty, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was earnings yield (-0.66)

runnersUp.name: Magnite, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was cash conversion (-0.24)

runnersUp.name: RingCentral, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was cash conversion (-1.15)

stock.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 55.6× trailing earnings and a 3.4% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot. growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +53.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $72.56 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-09-30, 50 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 50 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-19.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-10) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.excerpt: Store and retrieve data with Python, SQLite, and SQLAlchemy. You'll compare flat files with SQL and work with your data as Python objects.

stories.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
stories.excerpt: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.
stories.lead:
A federal judge has extended her block on construction of President Trump's D.C. arch for two weeks, another short-term victory for those who don't want to see the 250-foot structure break ground.

D.C. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended her temporary restraining order on Wednesday, the day before it was set to expire. She originally stepped in to block construction on the night of Nov. 5, after the National Capital Planning Commission and National Park Service gave the arch final approval and the Trump administration said construction could begin imminently.

stories.title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back
stories.excerpt: Shark Tank's Kevin O'Leary is among the big investors looking to Canada as a data centre development destination, while his US project faces local opposition.
stories.lead:
As Americans have grown increasingly sour on artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development, Canada's industry leaders are sensing an opportunity.

"Data centres in Canada looking pretty appealing right now," Lucy Hargreaves, CEO of non-profit policy group Build Canada, wrote on X the day after American voters passed 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives aimed at limiting or preventing data centre development in this month's midterm elections.

While the number of proposed AI data centres in the US dwarfs that of its northern neighbour, in recent months Canada is being increasingly pitched as a hub for these so-called "hyperscale" projects.

stories.title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
stories.excerpt: People stocking up on long-life food drove retail sales higher October, according to official data.
stories.lead:
Retail sales rose in October, driven by people buying long-life food such as tinned goods and UHT milk, according to official figures, external.

Sales volumes were 0.7% higher as people responded to the government's emergency preparedness "Be Ready" campaign, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.

The campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

Anthropic’s historic IPO yesterday certainly lived up to the hype, ending the day at a whopping $1.7tn valuation – but it looks like has failed to allay investor concerns around an AI bubble.

stories.title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?
stories.excerpt: Would AI be a good judge of whether you should get a mortgage, car loan or mobile phone contract?
stories.lead:
Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.

Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.

"When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent. But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report. It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit. When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.

With many of the company’s founders, investors and employees now worth billions of dollars – and demand for the company’s stock remaining resilient – attention now turns to the stability of the wider market, and the global headwinds that experts say could threaten the AI industry over the coming months.
